channel.title: The San Francisco Standard - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The San Francisco Standard (sfstandard.com)

item.title: ‘Get some new shoes, too, b****’: Marin hospital board meeting erupts ahead of strike
item.description: A MarinHealth board chair cursed out a union leader during public comment days before 1,200 workers launched a strike over costs.

item.title: What Steph Curry’s lingering knee injury means for the Warriors
item.description: As its superstar guard deals with a “tricky” injury, Golden State is preparing for Kristaps Porzingis to make his team debut.

item.title: How do Buster Posey’s Giants use data? We asked the team’s analytics guru
item.description: Longtime front office staffer Paul Bien was promoted to assistant general manager of baseball analytics in December.

item.title: Dems gone wild at Moscone Center. Plus: Beya Alcaraz faces more legal trouble
item.description: Also in today’s Power Play: Supervisor Stephen Sherrill faces heat over Bloomberg allegations.

item.title: Google’s AI bot said, ‘I’m gonna delete myself.’ An entire conference lost sleep over it
item.description: At the Sentient Futures Summit, AI engineers, ethicists, and lawyers debated the (non) human rights of AI workers.

item.title: Can SF’s theaters save Mid-Market? This lawmaker says it’s showtime
item.description: Supervisor Bilal Mahmood wants to revive the troubled corridor by gussying up its arts venues and streets, using private funding.

item.title: AI writes the code now. What’s left for software engineers?
item.description: Hiring is down, AI tools are in, and engineers fear they’re sliding toward a “permanent underclass.”

item.title: Salvation Army asks $58M for Mission land. Market-rate housing developers are lining up
item.description: The international charity says no San Francisco programs will be eliminated due to a sale.

item.title: Tahoe avalanche updates: Six moms, one from San Francisco, identified as victims
item.description: A spokesperson for several families named the victims as Carrie Atkin, Liz Clabaugh, Danielle Keatley, Kate Morse, Caroline Sekar, and Kate Vitt.

item.title: Oakland’s Alysa Liu wins gold, and everyone wants in on the celebration
item.description: From Gov. Gavin Newsom to BART, all eyes are on the U.S. figure skater.
